mom:
An approved IFC specifications for coal shed corrugated sheets, their installation scheme and associated materials as per Sub-Soc(M) dated 23-Jul-24 and 15-Aug-24 were issued. However,during mockup of sheets installation, following were the observations
1. The recommended sealant material (Mastic- Zahabiya / Foster brand) were applied but both have poor adhesion with PVDF coating and solidifying immediately. It will not serve the sealing purpose on overlapping as predicted. Moreover, a local vendor of Zahabiya was called at a plant site seeking his technical advice and he confirmed that the material is not suitable for intended use / purpose. It's just a sealing material that has no role in corrosion protection. The vendor has also informed that they have never applied this material as overlap joint with 06 inches width, they just use it to cover water ingress points based on inspection, if required.
2. No application of mastic material is observed on corrugated sheets designed, supplied and installed for different locations by different vendors (Mamut, NHI & HHI etc) for coal power plant. However, the same applies on corrugated sheets (Aluzinc) installed at FFBL for Urea / DAP storage building (controlled environment) due to stringent requirement of moisture sealing owing to the hygroscopic nature of the stored products, where mastic material is used in between with application of double tape for sealing.
3. Based on the inspection report as issued by Inspection unit, the corrosion was started from inside due to coal off gases and elongation of rivets holes due to vibrations. External water was not the cause of corrosion initiation & aggravation.
4. Due to sheets manufacturing process limitation, Top / bottom edges of supplied sheets are without galvanization & PVDF coating (protection) and can be a triggering point of corrosion. Needs to provide adequate protection against corrosion.
5. Rivets are protected from the top side with rubber seals, leaving the bottom side exposed to harsh environment (coal off gases), therefore, needs adequate protection from bottom side as well.
After detailed deliberations on the above points & review of previous MoMs, the following actions were agreed upon and approved,

meetingAgenda: Boilers' Center Pipe Replacement / Modification
mom:
FPCL CFB Boilers have two hot cyclones each for separation of large unburnt coal particles via cyclone separation process. Inside each of these hot cyclones, a center pipe is installed. Since ATA-2023, multiple types of defects have been observed in the center pipes cyclones of both the boilers in vicinity of the pipe supports after insertion of ceramic wool inside the space provided for expansion of pipes; the same was recommended by the Refractory OEM. In year 2024, a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) was performed aiming to find the cause of the failures and to subsequently take necessary actions for ensuring the reliability of the boilers w.r.t center pipes.
Subsequently, the matter was taken up with M/s HPS, who identified the wool filling in expansion Spare as a root cause of the defects in center pipes and recommended corrective actions, which were implemented in the center pipes during ATA-2025. Additionally, metallographic analysis was performed on the center pipes. The results show the initial findings—namely, Sigma Phase Embrittlement and Creep—as the causes of the defects. The RCA, along with the case history, was presented during the subject Technical Session to finalize the job scope for ATA-2026.
Following actions were assigned against the presentation delivered by PTE:

mom:
FPCL CFB Boilers have two hot cyclones each for separation of large unburnt coal particles via cyclone separation process. Inside each of these hot cyclones, a center pipe is installed.
Since ATA-2023, multiple types of failures have been observed in the center pipes of both the boilers in vicinity of the pipe supports. causes of the failures. The RCA, along with the case history, was presented during a
Technical Session (F/T/TSM/0137) dated 30th May, 2025. The subject Technical Session was
held to present the working against the actions assigned in the last session and finalize the
way-forward for ATA-2026.

The Bottom Ash from the furnace is discharged through three (03) ash chutes that pass through the air plenum chamber. These ash chutes are enclosed within a casing located inside the wind box. During boiler operation, ash particles accumulate within the ash chute casing due to wear or damage of the ash chutes. This accumulated ash is drained through a 2" pipe provided at the bottom of the ash chute casing during plant turnarounds.

Since the boiler operates continuously throughout the year, damage to the ash chutes often occurs during operation, leading to ash deposition and subsequent choking of the 2" drain line. To clear such blockages, the drain line is typically cut at two locations for manual de-choking and then re-welded after cleaning.

To eliminate the need for repetitive cutting and welding, a Mechanical package is developed to install Threaded flanged joints at two locations on the 2" drain line for easy removal and reinstaliation.

mom:
The three (03) numbers of 24" exhaust lines connected to the STG-04 condenser PSVs are currently supported only at their far end by a fixed structural support, while the PSV side is flanged and directly attached to the PSVs. During each TA, these PSVs are removed for PM and calibration. Once the valves are removed, the flanged ends of the exhaust lines become unsupported and are temporarily rested on scaffolding pipes.
This temporary arrangement introduces safety concerns as the scaffolding is erected based on experience without any structural load calculations, posing a risk of instability or failure. Additionally, deflection of the scaffolding pipes makes it difficult to realign the heavy 24" exhaust lines with the PSVs during reinstallation, resulting in increased time and effort.
To eliminate these hazards and maintenance challenges, It is proposed to install permanent structural supports near the flanged ends of the exhaust lines, similar to the arrangement already installed on 24MW STGs.
